instructions:
Read the paper below and produce a structured summary.

It matched these tracked topics; `relevance` must contain one entry per slug, stating what this paper changes for that topic:
- overthinking: Overthinking — When and why large reasoning models think more than a problem needs (or less than it needs) — the accuracy/efficiency tradeoff of reasoning length, test-time compute scaling, and methods to make a model stop, or keep going, at the right point.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

concepts: string - reusable ideas this paper relies on or introduces
datasets: string - datasets, benchmarks, corpora or simulators used
output_schema.limitations: string - stated limits plus any the reader should notice
output_schema.method: string - how it works, enough for a reader to explain it
methods: string - named methods, architectures or algorithms
output_schema.one_liner: string - what the paper does, in one sentence, no hype
output_schema.problem: string - the problem it addresses and why it is open

relevance.<topic-slug>: string - why this matters for that specific topic

output_schema.results: string - headline numbers, on which benchmarks, against what

contributions: Test-time scaling procedure that samples and evaluates multiple candidate GUI actions before committing to one
Reinforcement learning approach that rewards successful clicks on interface elements to improve grounding accuracy
Claimed state-of-the-art results on GUI grounding and task execution benchmarks
result.limitations: Not stated in the available material (abstract only; no PDF attached).
result.method: GTA1 applies test-time scaling by sampling multiple candidate action sequences for a GUI task and evaluating them to pick the best one, and separately trains element grounding with reinforcement learning that rewards clicks landing successfully on the intended interface element.
result.one_liner: A GUI agent that samples and judges multiple candidate actions at test time and uses RL-trained click rewards to ground actions on interface elements more precisely.
result.problem: GUI agents must select the right action from a large space of possibilities and precisely target visual elements in complex interfaces; the paper addresses both action selection and grounding accuracy.

relevance.overthinking: Only shares the phrase 'test-time scaling' with the topic. Here it refers to sampling and judging multiple candidate GUI actions for element grounding, not to calibrating how long a model reasons or trading off chain-of-thought length against accuracy. No treatment of reasoning-length, stopping criteria, or compute/accuracy tradeoffs for reasoning models. Tangential keyword match only.

result.results: Abstract claims state-of-the-art results on GUI grounding and task execution benchmarks; no specific benchmark names or numeric scores are given in the available material.
